headline: Timed Access for Waterfall Corridor and Mountain Stays
reservation: While Hood River is an open town, neighboring attractions like Multnomah Falls may require seasonal timed-use permits for vehicle entry. Camping near Mount Hood and popular fruit-harvest farm events should be reserved well in advance; always check the U.S. Forest Service and Oregon State Parks websites for current land-use fees and road status.

days.title: Riverfront and Wind Sports
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Downtown Hood River

stops.name: Hood River Event Site
stops.detail: Watch kiteboarders and windsurfers harness the Gorge winds from the safety of the shoreline walking path.

stops.name: Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail
stops.detail: Walk or cycle a paved segment of the historic road for elevated views of the Columbia River.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; very compact town center
days.note: Waterfront areas are exceptionally windy; secure hats and loose items.

days.title: The Fruit Loop Harvest

stops.name: Hood River Fruit Loop
stops.detail: Drive the scenic 35-mile loop through the valley, stopping at various farm stands for seasonal pears, apples, or blossoms.

stops.name: Parkdale
stops.detail: A small mountain community offering clear-day views of Mount Hood’s north face.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the full circuit; stop durations vary
days.note: Orchards are private property; only enter designated u-pick or visitor areas.

days.title: Basalt Walls and Waterfalls

stops.name: Mosier Plateau Trail
stops.detail: Hike the ridge for views of the river and seasonal wildflowers like balsamroot and lupine.

stops.name: Western Antique Aeroplane and Automobile Museum
stops.detail: Explore a massive collection of vintage transportation housed in hangars near the local airfield.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; I-84 traffic can be heavy near Mosier
days.note: Wildflower seasons are brief and vary annually; stay on trails to protect the fragile bloom.

intel.title: Trailhead Demand
intel.text: Parking at popular Gorge trailheads often fills by 9 AM on summer weekends. Consider using local shuttles if available for the waterfall corridor.

intel.title: Mountain Shadows
intel.text: Signal is reliable in Hood River but drops significantly on Route 35 and deeper Gorge trails. Keep offline maps for the Fruit Loop navigation.

intel.title: Gorge Service Hubs
intel.text: Hood River and The Dalles are the primary locations for fuel. Ensure you have a full tank before heading south toward the Mount Hood wilderness areas.

intel.title: Orchard Bloom
intel.text: The timing of fruit blossoms in April and harvest in October depends on spring temperatures. Check the Fruit Loop official calendar for current stand hours.

intel.title: Road Conditions
intel.text: Interstate 84 and Route 35 can experience sudden closures due to weather or landslides. Check TripCheck Oregon for real-time transportation updates.

plan.arrival: Arrive via PDX, drive east on I-84 through the Gorge, and settle into your Hood River base; allow extra time for the scenic approach.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal; winter visits toward Mount Hood require traction tires or chains by law.
plan.goldenHour: Rowena Crest Viewpoint offers a classic sunset vista over the Gorge loops, a short drive east of town.
